title: Hosted SSE transient-silence diagnostics & customer recovery playbook
creator: Asha Menon
description:
Summary: Multiple tenants have reported mid-request silent periods on Hosted API SSE streams where the server stops emitting tokens for 5–45 seconds and then either resumes a partial continuation or the connection terminates without a deterministic final token. Symptoms include duplicated early tokens on resume, missing finalizers (no EOF event), and client-visible truncated transcripts. This ticket captures triage findings, temporary mitigations applied, proposed fixes, and a rollout/runbook for production recovery and verification.

Observed pattern: incidents cluster tightly around autoscaling events (worker recycle or kernel switchover), edge proxy restarts, and occasional high-KV-cache churn. Network-level traces show TCP connections remaining open while no application-level frames are emitted. Sampling indicates 18 distinct tenants affected between 2026-02-24 and 2026-02-28, ~0.6% of streaming traffic during those windows.

Hypothesis: a sequence of coupled factors — (1) serving runtime flush policy that defers finalization when output queue is below a threshold, (2) edge proxy backpressure or HTTP/2 multiplex quiesce that interrupts event flush scheduling, and (3) client SDK heuristics that assume final EOF marker presence — results in a midstream silence that the client interprets as an infinite wait.

Goal: Provide immediate mitigations to reduce customer impact, implement deterministic server-side finalization and probe instrumentation, ship SDK resilience updates, add e2e tests, and verify via canary and tenant-level smoke checks.
comments: 2026-03-01 - Asha Menon: Incident received from AcmeVault support; initial triage shows long silent gaps in SSE stream with no error frames. Created ticket and notified SRE/Edge/Runtime owners.

2026-03-02 - Jonah Park: Collected example traces (trace IDs: trace-20260302-88a3, trace-20260302-9b1f). Noted worker recycle at 10:13 UTC aligned with silence windows. Uploaded packet captures and SDK logs to Drive: https://drive.redwood/company/hosted-sse-silence/2026-03-packets.zip

2026-03-03 - SRE (Lena Rodriguez): Applied temporary mitigation in us-west2: enabled aggressive keepalive and reduced proxy connection draining window from 30s to 3s for streaming routes. Observed 70% reduction in recurrence for customers behind that edge.
2026-03-05 - Jonah Park: Deployed runtime hotfix candidate to dev cluster: force_emit_finalizer_on_drain=true. Unit tests added. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/7832

2026-03-07 - Customer Escalation Call: Walked through playbook with AcmeVault; agreed to run canary in their tenant for two hours. They requested detailed mitigation steps and audit logs during the window.

2026-03-10 - QA (Priya Kaur): Added e2e harness that simulates edge restart mid-stream and validates resume token integrity. Tests failing intermittently under high-concurrency mode; investigating race on session finalization path.

2026-03-12 - Jonah Park: Introduced a diagnostic probe that emits last-token timestamp events and an "idle-sentinel" frame when the server has been silent for >2s. Telemetry metric name: sse.last_emit_age_ms and sse.idle_sentinel_emitted (counter).

2026-03-14 - Oncall (Marco Silva): Canary results: us-west2 canary with hotfix enabled showed 0 repros for 72h across 12k streams. Plan to schedule staged rollout across all regions with rollback plan.

Artifacts: Confluence runbook: https://confluence.redwood/hosted-sse-silent-runbook | PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-js/pull/451 | Telemetry dashboard: https://dash.redwood/boards/hosted-sse-silence
acceptance_criteria: Production metric sse.last_emit_age_ms 95th percentile for streaming routes reduced to <200ms under normal load (measured over 24h)
No customer-visible silent mid-request incidents for 7 consecutive days across a 10% traffic canary and then 100% rollout
SDK patch released that detects and resumes on idle-sentinel within 500ms and produces a deterministic resume/log message
E2E harness reproduces the previously failing scenario deterministically and remains stable in CI under 50 concurrent streams
Runbook and customer-facing postmortem drafted and reviewed by SRE, Runtime, Edge, and Support
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Use internal streaming harness (tools/stream-sim) to start a long-running SSE request emitting a token every 100ms
2) Trigger an edge proxy restart or simulate TCP quiesce at midstream (tools/edge-probe --quiesce-at=2000ms)
3) Observe client-side SDK behavior: measure last received token timestamp, whether EOF frame is received, and if resume token is present
4) Compare runtime logs for worker drain events and flush scheduling entries (log lines containing 'drain:finalize' or 'kvcache:reap')
5) Run with kernel-switch variant to capture any change in kernel scheduling impact
mitigation_plan: Short term (applied): reduce proxy drain window, enable aggressive keepalive on streaming routes, and provide customers with a temporary tenant canary flag
Hotfix: runtime change to always emit an idle-sentinel frame if no token emitted for >2s during active stream; force flush finalizer on session drain
SDK update: on receipt of idle-sentinel, SDK should start exponential resume probes with resume-token, surface a clear diagnostic log, and fallback to reconnect after N attempts
Telemetry: add sse.last_emit_age_ms and sse.idle_sentinel_emitted metrics and a dedicated dashboard and alert (P1) when 95p > 2s
Long term: remove reliance on heuristics by implementing explicit server-side session checkpoints and strong ordering guarantees for resume tokens; add contract tests between SDK and runtime
implementation_notes:
Code changes: runtime: introduce emit_idle_sentinel flag and finalize-on-drain path change in StreamSessionManager (files: stream/session_manager.cc, stream/flusher.cc). Add unit tests for finalize ordering and idempotent finalizer. SDKs: add idle-sentinel handler and resume-probe sequence (sdk-js and sdk-py PRs). Observability: add two histogram metrics and wire them into the console board.

Testing and rollout: create canary job that routes 5% of traffic from low-risk tenants for 48h, validate telemetry and customer feedback, then rollout region-by-region (us-west2 -> eu-west1 -> us-east1 -> ap-southeast1). Rollback: toggle emit_idle_sentinel=false and revert proxy drain window to 30s.

Risk and tradeoffs: emitting sentinel frames increases token emission events and may marginally increase cost for extremely high-volume short streams. However customer impact and correctness trade favor stronger signals. Ensure circuit-breaker thresholds to avoid amplification during cascading failures.

Follow-ups: postmortem due by 2026-03-25, add permanent contract test to CI, and propose a Dedicated/Private deployment checklist for kernel/worker lifecycle to avoid similar regressions in non-hosted environments.
owner_notes: Jonah: prioritize telemetry dashboards before wide rollout. If dashboard shows >0.1% tenants still experiencing 2s+ silence after canary, pause and investigate
SRE: ensure oncall playbook includes a quick toggle for proxy drain window and tenant canary flag
